content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "To increase the likelihood of success, one should set realistic goals and work persistently towards them." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
content.topic: Setting realistic goals and working persistently towards success

modelEssay.title: Setting Realistic Goals and Working Persistently Towards Success
modelEssay.content:
To increase the likelihood of success, one should set realistic goals and work persistently towards them. This adage is not only a guiding principle but also a reflection of the journey to success. Setting realistic goals provides a clear direction and prevents one from wandering aimlessly. Moreover, persistent work is the catalyst that transforms dreams into reality.

For instance, when Thomas Edison invented the light bulb, he faced numerous failures. However, his unwavering commitment to his goal led him to eventual success. Similarly, in my own life, setting attainable goals for my studies and consistently striving to achieve them has significantly improved my academic performance.

In conclusion, setting realistic goals and working persistently towards them is the key to unlocking our potential. It is not the size of the goal that matters, but the determination and effort we put into achieving it.

structureAnalysis.paragraph1: 引入段：引用名言，提出观点，即设定现实目标和坚持不懈地努力是成功的关键
structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：举例说明（爱迪生发明电灯）和个人经历（设定学习目标）来支持观点
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：重申观点，强调目标的大小不是关键，而是实现目标的决心和努力

highlights: 使用了'To increase the likelihood of success'等高级表达
运用了举例论证，增强说服力
逻辑清晰，过渡自然（This adage is not only..., Moreover, In conclusion）
词汇丰富，避免重复（setting realistic goals, persistent work, catalyst）

transcript.text: Logging into your email account can sometimes feel like trying to hack into the Pentagon.
transcript.translation: 登录你的电子邮箱账户有时感觉就像试图入侵五角大楼。

transcript.text: If you follow all of the guidelines, you need to use a different password for every one of your accounts, use an incomprehensible variety of letters, numbers and symbols, sign up for two-step verification, and change every password every time one of them is compromised.
transcript.translation: 如果你遵循所有指南，你需要为每个账户使用不同的密码，使用令人费解的字母、数字和符号组合，注册两步验证，并在每次密码泄露时更改所有密码。

transcript.text: More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being.
transcript.translation: 很多时候，你还需要选择包含街道标志的照片，因为这显然为你的电脑提供了确凿证据，证明你实际上是一个人类。

transcript.text: It's no small wonder most of us forget our passwords more often than our keys.
transcript.translation: 难怪我们大多数人忘记密码的频率比忘记钥匙还要高。

transcript.text: Now, a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon.
transcript.translation: 现在，芬兰阿尔托大学的研究人员进行的一项新的同行评审研究正试图找出我们忘记密码的原因，以帮助终结这一令人沮丧的现象。

transcript.text: Their findings suggest that how likely you are to remember your password has less to do with the intricacy of the password itself, and more to do with how often you anticipate using it.
transcript.translation: 他们的发现表明，你记住密码的可能性与密码本身的复杂性关系不大，而更多地与你预期使用它的频率有关。

transcript.text: Which is to say, you are far more likely to remember a complicated password if you know you'll frequently be using it to log into an account than you are to remember a simple password for an account that you don't expect to log into very often.
transcript.translation: 也就是说，如果你知道你会频繁使用一个复杂密码登录账户，那么你记住它的可能性远远大于记住一个你预计不常登录的简单密码。

transcript.text: The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often in order to help them remember their secret codes.
transcript.translation: 研究人员建议网站增加更多激励措施，鼓励用户更频繁地登录，以帮助他们记住密码。

transcript.text: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.
transcript.translation: 牛津大学已得出结论，所有社会都由七条普遍的道德规则维系，其中包括尊重上级和尊重他人财产。

transcript.text: Although many cultures are moving towards more liberal, less hierarchical organizations, the new research suggests that traditional power structures and basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies.
transcript.translation: 尽管许多文化正朝着更自由、等级更少的组织形式发展，但新研究表明，传统的权力结构以及慈善和博爱的基本价值观是成功社会的基石。

transcript.text: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes.
transcript.translation: 这项对全球60种不同文化的大规模研究发现，所有社区都在七条基本道德准则下运作。

transcript.text: Those universal rules are help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others.
transcript.translation: 这些普遍规则是帮助你的家庭、帮助你的群体、回报恩惠、勇敢、尊重上级、公平分配资源，以及尊重他人财产。

transcript.text: The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter-gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found.
transcript.translation: 研究人员发现，这些特质存在于每一种社区中，无论是传统的狩猎采集者还是先进的文明，它们有助于维护文明社会并促进社会合作。

transcript.text: Everyone, everywhere, shares a common moral code, said Dr.
transcript.translation: 每个人、每个地方都共享一套共同的道德准则，博士说。

transcript.text: Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford.
transcript.translation: 奥利弗·斯科特·柯里，牛津大学的首席作者和高级研究员。

transcript.text: These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures because people face the same social problems.
transcript.translation: 这七条道德规则似乎在所有文化中都是普遍的，因为人们面临着相同的社会问题。

transcript.text: Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something.
transcript.translation: 即使其中一些特质看起来像右翼或保守派，例如尊重权威，左翼人士仍然会有群体忠诚和对某人或某事的尊重。

transcript.text: This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us.
transcript.translation: 这表明，真正团结我们的东西比分裂我们的更多。

transcript.text: The study, published in Current Anthropology, is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
transcript.translation: 这项发表在《当前人类学》上的研究，是有史以来进行的最大规模、最全面和最广泛的道德调查，旨在查明不同社会是否有不同版本的道德。

transcript.text: The team accessed the world's best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60 societies around the world.
transcript.translation: 该团队访问了世界上最好的档案库，分析了来自全球60个社会的600多个来源的记录。

transcript.text: They found that the seven rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions, and politics.
transcript.translation: 他们发现，这七条规则在所有社会中都被认为是道德良善的，并且在所有大陆、宗教和政治中都得到遵守。

transcript.text: However, some communities valued certain rules more highly than others.
transcript.translation: 然而，一些社区比其他社区更看重某些规则。

transcript.text: Dr.
transcript.translation: 博士。

transcript.text: Curry hopes that this research helps to promote mutual understanding between people of different cultures and appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ.
transcript.translation: 柯里希望这项研究有助于促进不同文化背景的人们之间的相互理解，并欣赏我们的共同点以及我们如何及为何不同。

transcript.text: Co-author Professor Harvey Whitehouse said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field rather than relying on old data.
transcript.translation: 合著者哈维·怀特豪斯教授表示，社会科学家现在应该开始在实地测试该理论，而不是依赖旧数据。

transcript.text: This study was based on historical descriptions of cultures around the world, he said.
transcript.translation: 他说，这项研究基于对全球文化的历史描述。

transcript.text: These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing.
transcript.translation: 这些描述是在我们正在测试的理论独立且之前进行的。

transcript.text: In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data more systematically out in the field.
transcript.translation: 未来，如果社会科学家认真对待测试道德理论，他们将需要更系统地在实地收集新数据。

transcript.text: When it comes to food, color is money.
transcript.translation: 说到食物，颜色就是金钱。

transcript.text: Food companies know that better color gives better prices, so they ensure that their products are attractive in color to bolster earnings.
transcript.translation: 食品公司知道更好的颜色能带来更高的价格，因此他们确保产品颜色诱人，以增加收益。

transcript.text: Oranges, for example, have to meet specific color standards, and oranges are just the beginning.
transcript.translation: 例如，橘子必须符合特定的颜色标准，而橘子只是开始。

transcript.text: There are color standards for foods including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey, and cherries.
transcript.translation: 对于食物，包括炸薯条、西红柿、南瓜、橄榄、蜂蜜和樱桃，都有颜色标准。

transcript.text: The attention to color is for good reason.
transcript.translation: 对颜色的关注是有充分理由的。

transcript.text: For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience.
transcript.translation: 尽管舌头被频繁提及，但我们的眼睛可能才是饮食体验中最重要的部分。

transcript.text: A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties, and the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.
transcript.translation: 我们大脑的大部分功能都用于处理视觉，而只有一两个百分点用于味觉官能，结果是颜色实际上改变了我们品尝食物的方式。

transcript.text: Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste.
transcript.translation: 科学家多次证明了颜色对味道的重要性。

transcript.text: In a 1980 study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage.
transcript.translation: 例如，在1980年的一项研究中，测试参与者被要求在不看到饮料的情况下说出他们正在喝的饮料的味道。

transcript.text: Only one in five was able to identify it as orange.
transcript.translation: 只有五分之一的人能够识别出它是橙子味。

transcript.text: But when they were allowed to see what they were drinking, which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor.
transcript.translation: 但当他们被允许看到所喝的饮料是橙色时，每个人都识别出了橙子味。

transcript.text: And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange.
transcript.translation: 当一种青柠味的饮料被染成橙色时，近一半的受访者将饮料的味道识别为橙子味。

transcript.text: None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color.
transcript.translation: 当饮料是绿色时，没有人犯这种错误。

transcript.text: What's happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a beverage they can't see, or that has an abnormal color?
transcript.translation: 当某人无法识别看不到或颜色异常的饮料的味道时，发生了什么？

transcript.text: Is it that participants can't discern what the flavor is, and so rely on visual cues?
transcript.translation: 是因为参与者无法辨别味道，因此依赖视觉线索吗？

transcript.text: Or does color actually change the experience of taste?
transcript.translation: 还是颜色实际上改变了味觉体验？

transcript.text: The key to these questions is the effect of color on expectation.
transcript.translation: 这些问题的关键是颜色对期望的影响。

transcript.text: The brain makes predictions using color.
transcript.translation: 大脑使用颜色进行预测。

transcript.text: These predictions rely on expectations that come from experience.
transcript.translation: 这些预测依赖于来自经验的期望。

transcript.text: Research shows that we're all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them.
transcript.translation: 研究表明，我们生来就喜欢甜食，并渴望食用它们。

transcript.text: But we aren't born knowing what the sweet things we crave look like, so we need to learn this over time.
transcript.translation: 但我们生来并不知道我们渴望的甜食是什么样子，所以我们需要随着时间学习这一点。

transcript.text: The brain gets information from the environment, and we learn, for example, that fruits go from green and sour to red and ripe and sweet.
transcript.translation: 大脑从环境中获取信息，我们学习到，例如，水果从绿色和酸涩变为红色、成熟和甜美。

transcript.text: Thus, if we see a green berry, we equate its color with a sour taste, and just looking at a red fruit will activate our expectations that it will taste sweet and delicious.
transcript.translation: 因此，如果我们看到一个绿色的浆果，我们会将其颜色与酸味等同起来，而仅仅看到红色水果就会激活我们对其味道甜美可口的期望。

transcript.text: Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives.
transcript.translation: 寻找意义是许多人在一生中都会经历的事情。

transcript.text: For some, this meaning is religious, some political, and some interpersonal.
transcript.translation: 对一些人来说，这种意义是宗教的，对一些人是政治的，对一些人是人际关系的。

transcript.text: And having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness.
transcript.translation: 拥有一种意义感可以带给我们幸福。

transcript.text: A new study looks at the relationship between meaning and happiness in the context of financial resources.
transcript.translation: 一项新研究探讨了意义与幸福之间的关系，背景是经济资源。

transcript.text: Rhea Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning.
transcript.translation: 来自多伦多大学的Rhea Catapano及其同事发现，意义对富人幸福感的预测远弱于对穷人，这表明经济资源会影响我们如何体验意义。

transcript.text: The team analyzed data from over 500,000 people across 123 countries.
transcript.translation: 该团队分析了来自123个国家超过50万人的数据。

transcript.text: The first study used data from a daily poll of U.
transcript.translation: 第一项研究使用了来自每日民意调查的数据，针对美国

transcript.text: S.
transcript.translation: 美国

transcript.text: residents collected between 2013 and 2015.
transcript.translation: 居民数据收集于2013年至2015年间。

transcript.text: Well-being was tracked using measures of positive affect, whether during the day, before they were surveyed, participants had smiled or laughed a lot, or experienced a lot of happiness.
transcript.translation: 通过积极情感的指标来跟踪幸福感，即在调查前的一天内，参与者是否经常微笑或大笑，或体验到很多幸福。

transcript.text: Meaning was measured through a daily purpose index, which explored the extent to which participants felt that they like what they do every day and are motivated to achieve their goals.
transcript.translation: 意义通过一个每日目标指数来衡量，该指数探讨了参与者感觉喜欢每天所做的事情以及有动力实现目标的程度。

transcript.text: Finally, income levels were assessed.
transcript.translation: 最后，评估了收入水平。

transcript.text: The results showed that the correlation between meaning and happiness was strongest among those in lower income brackets.
transcript.translation: 结果显示，意义与幸福之间的相关性在低收入人群中最为强烈。

transcript.text: But as income levels increased, the correlation became weaker.
transcript.translation: 但随着收入水平的提高，相关性变得更弱。

transcript.text: The second study looked at worldwide data.
transcript.translation: 第二项研究考察了全球数据。

transcript.text: Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study, while meaning was measured using the single question.
transcript.translation: 幸福使用与第一项研究相同的问题来衡量，而意义使用单一问题来衡量。

transcript.text: Do you feel your life has an important purpose or meaning?
transcript.translation: 你觉得你的生活有重要的目标或意义吗？

transcript.text: Again, the strength of the relationship between meaning and happiness depended on participants' income.
transcript.translation: 同样，意义与幸福之间关系的强度取决于参与者的收入。

transcript.text: Meaning had a greater influence on happiness for those on lower incomes compared to those in higher brackets.
transcript.translation: 与收入较高的人相比，意义对低收入者的幸福有更大的影响。

transcript.text: In the final study, French participants indicated the extent to which they felt they led a purposeful and meaningful life, and how much they considered themselves a happy person.
transcript.translation: 在最后一项研究中，法国参与者表示了他们感觉自己过着有目标和有意义的生活的程度，以及他们在多大程度上认为自己是一个幸福的人。

transcript.text: Finally, rather than using specific income brackets, they placed themselves on a social ladder, representing where they stand in society with regard to wealth, education, and career.
transcript.translation: 最后，不是使用特定的收入范围，而是让他们将自己放在一个社会阶梯上，代表他们在社会中相对于财富、教育和职业的地位。

transcript.text: The results from this study duplicated those of the first two.
transcript.translation: 这项研究的结果重复了前两项研究的结果。

transcript.text: So, overall, meaning and happiness had a stronger relationship in those with fewer resources than those with more.
transcript.translation: 因此，总体而言，意义与幸福在资源较少的人群中关系更强，而不是在资源较多的人群中。

transcript.text: This might be the case because richer individuals have more access to other sources of happiness, many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community.
transcript.translation: 这可能是因为富人有更多的其他幸福来源，其中许多是外部的，比如没有压力或社区。

transcript.text: Thus, a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose, or meaning is less important.
transcript.translation: 因此，关注内在的满足感、目标或意义就不那么重要了。

questionGroups.title: Are forgotten crops the future of food?

material.title: Are forgotten crops the future of food?

paragraphs.text: On a small fruit farm near the Straits of Malacca, Lim Kok Ann is down to just one tree growing kedondong, a crunchy, sour berry that Malaysians mostly use in pickles (腌菜) and salads. "It's not very well-known," says the 45-year-old, who is instead focusing on longan (龙眼) berries and pineapples, which have bigger markets. "We have to grow what is profitable," he says.
paragraphs.translation: 在马六甲海峡附近的一个小型水果农场，林国恩只剩下一棵种植kedondong的树，这是一种脆而酸的浆果，马来西亚人大多用于腌菜和沙拉。"它不太出名，"这位45岁的人说，他转而专注于龙眼和菠萝，这些有更大的市场。"我们必须种植有利可图的东西，"他说。

paragraphs.text: But less than an hour away in the Malaysian countryside, inside three giant, silver domes, scientists are trying to change the future of food. They're pushing the boundaries of what humans eat by growing and processing so-called 'alternative' crops—such as kedondong. At the headquarters of global research centre Crops For the Future (CFF) this particular under-used fruit has been turned into a sugar-free juice, high in vitamin C and getting top marks in sensory evaluations. "Anything you see here is a forgotten crop," says Sayed Azam-Ali of the abundant plants weaving through the gardens of CFF outside Malaysia's capital Kuala Lumpur.
paragraphs.translation: 但在马来西亚乡村不到一小时车程的地方，在三个巨大的银色穹顶内，科学家们正试图改变食品的未来。他们通过种植和加工所谓的"替代"作物来拓宽人类饮食的边界——例如kedondong。在全球研究中心Crops For the Future (CFF)的总部，这种特别未被充分利用的水果已被制成果汁，富含维生素C，并在感官评价中获得最高分。"你在这里看到的任何东西都是被遗忘的作物，"Sayed Azam-Ali说，他指的是CFF花园中缠绕的丰富植物，该中心位于马来西亚首都吉隆坡郊外。

paragraphs.text: Prof Azam-Ali explains that just four crops—wheat, maize, rice and soybean—provide two-thirds of the world's food supply. "We're dependent on these four," he says. "But actually there's 7,000 crops we've been farming for thousands of years. We ignore all of those." Researchers are trying to unlock the potential of these ignored crops—plants they describe as forgotten, under-used or 'alternative' as they are displaced by increasingly uniform diets fuelled by processed ingredients from the major crops.
paragraphs.translation: Azam-Ali教授解释说，只有四种作物——小麦、玉米、水稻和大豆——提供了世界三分之二的食物供应。"我们依赖这四种作物，"他说。"但实际上，我们种植了数千年的作物有7000种。我们忽略了所有这些。"研究人员正试图挖掘这些被忽视作物的潜力——这些植物被描述为被遗忘的、未被充分利用的或"替代的"，因为它们被由主要作物的加工成分驱动的日益统一的饮食所取代。

paragraphs.text: It's a timely quest. The food sector is already responsible for nearly a third of global greenhouse gas emissions. By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion. Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions.
paragraphs.translation: 这是一个及时的探索。食品部门已经占全球温室气体排放的近三分之一。到2050年，预计世界必须多生产50%的食物来养活预计的100亿全球人口。在不加剧气候变化的情况下满足这一需求需要紧急解决方案。

paragraphs.text: Forgotten crops hold key answers. By investing in neglected local plants, countries can reduce their reliance on imported crops and their carbon-heavy supply chains. Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate also boosts food security at a time warming climates threaten existing crops. On top of that forgotten crops are among the most climate-resilient (具有气候韧性的) and nutritious, argues Azam-Ali. His summary is plain: "Dietary diversification is critical to the future of humanity."
paragraphs.translation: 被遗忘的作物持有关键答案。通过投资于被忽视的本地植物，各国可以减少对进口作物及其高碳供应链的依赖。恢复人类曾经食用的作物多样性，也能在气候变暖威胁现有作物时增强粮食安全。此外，Azam-Ali认为，被遗忘的作物是最具气候韧性和营养的之一。他的总结很明确："饮食多样化对人类的未来至关重要。"

paragraphs.text: Food security experts agree. "There is no food insecurity in the world, there is food ignorance," says Cecilia Tortajada, a senior research fellow at the Institute of Water Policy at the National University of Singapore. "Whenever we have native crops we tend to disregard them as if they were not valuable but they are," she adds.
paragraphs.translation: 粮食安全专家表示同意。"世界上没有食物不安全，只有食物无知，"新加坡国立大学水政策研究所的高级研究员Cecilia Tortajada说。"每当我们有本地作物时，我们往往忽视它们，好像它们没有价值，但它们确实有，"她补充道。

paragraphs.text: Azam-Ali knows that scepticism firsthand. He came across alternative crops in the 1980s through the work of women farmers he met in Niger. The then-PhD student remembers marvelling at the crops they grew in their backyards, without the benefits of technology, to feed their families when the big crops failed. He saw a tremendous opportunity to build alternative food systems. But "the resistance was enormous," he recalls.
paragraphs.translation: Azam-Ali亲身了解这种怀疑。他在1980年代通过在尼日尔遇到的女农民的工作接触到了替代作物。这位当时的博士生记得，他惊叹于她们在后院种植的作物，没有技术的好处，却在主要作物歉收时养活了家人。他看到了建立替代食物系统的巨大机会。但"阻力巨大，"他回忆道。

paragraphs.text: Undeterred, he ploughed on. Project after project helped prove these crops were viable in different environments as alternatives to the staple ones. But the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained. "That's the critical thing," he says. In one of the centre's domes, food technologist Tan Xinlin uses powdered moringa (辣木) leaves in place of some wheat flour to bake a cake lower in gluten (谷胶) and higher in nutrients. Tan's job is to create recipes with these still-unfamiliar ingredients that will appeal to both local and international tastes. In recent years she has used some of the forgotten crops grown at CFF, such as moringa and bambara groundnut, to make everything from instant soup to Indian snacks. "I try to modernise forgotten crops instead of using old recipes," says Tan, who is also a trained chef. It's a strategy to appeal to the world's growing middle classes who are increasingly turning to the fast and processed food industries. It's also a way to help counter perceptions of local crops as "old or poor people's food" or as inferior "women's crops", adds Tan.
paragraphs.translation: 他毫不气馁，继续前进。一个又一个项目帮助证明这些作物在不同环境中作为主食作物的替代品是可行的。但这些作物是否有市场的问题仍然存在。"这是关键，"他说。在中心的一个穹顶内，食品技术专家谭欣琳使用辣木粉代替部分小麦粉，烘焙出低谷胶、高营养的蛋糕。谭的工作是创造使用这些仍然不熟悉的食谱，以吸引本地和国际口味。近年来，她使用了CFF种植的一些被遗忘的作物，如辣木和班巴拉花生，制作从速溶汤到印度小吃的各种食品。"我试图现代化被遗忘的作物，而不是使用旧食谱，"谭说，她也是一位训练有素的厨师。这是一种吸引世界不断增长的中产阶级的策略，他们越来越多地转向快餐和加工食品行业。谭补充说，这也是一种帮助抵消对本地作物作为"老人或穷人的食物"或劣等"女人的作物"的看法的方式。

paragraphs.text: The roots of these connotations about local foods can run deep. The bambara groundnut, a protein-rich native crop of sub-Saharan Africa that is also grown in parts of southeast Asia, can trace its marginalisation to colonial rule. "African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it," says Azam-Ali. "Colonial powers said you can't grow that because there's no oil. We can't get a market for it." But today the bambara murukku is one of CFF's best-reviewed foods and they are aiming to get it into grocery stores, pointing to the success of crops like quinoa to potential investors. Some 30 years ago, quinoa was virtually unheard of outside its native mountains in Bolivia and Peru. Today the nutritious grain is found on the menus of lavish restaurants across the world.
paragraphs.translation: 这些关于本地食物的内涵根源可能很深。班巴拉花生，一种蛋白质丰富的撒哈拉以南非洲本地作物，也在东南亚部分地区种植，其边缘化可以追溯到殖民统治。"种植班巴拉花生的非洲女性实际上因此受到惩罚，"Azam-Ali说。"殖民势力说你不能种那个，因为它没有油。我们无法为它找到市场。"但今天，班巴拉murukku是CFF评价最高的食物之一，他们正试图将其推向杂货店，向潜在投资者指出藜麦等作物的成功。大约30年前，藜麦在其本土的玻利维亚和秘鲁山区之外几乎无人知晓。今天，这种营养丰富的谷物出现在世界各地豪华餐厅的菜单上。

paragraphs.text: Measuring crops by nutrition instead of yield is at the heart of the forgotten foods enterprise. Ever since the "green revolution" of the 1960s, high-yielding crops have dominated modern agriculture. That was in part a crucial response to devastating famines at a time when the world needed to increase its food supply. Today "nutrition is becoming a time bomb", says Azam-Ali, as growing carbon dioxide levels strip crops of their minerals. Instead of bio-fortifying major crops we should be investing in those forgotten crops that are already more nutritious, he asserts.
paragraphs.translation: 以营养而非产量衡量作物是遗忘食品企业的核心。自1960年代的"绿色革命"以来，高产作物主导了现代农业。这在一定程度上是对毁灭性饥荒的关键回应，当时世界需要增加食物供应。今天，"营养正在成为定时炸弹，"Azam-Ali说，因为不断增长的二氧化碳水平剥夺了作物的矿物质。他断言，我们应该投资于那些已经更有营养的被遗忘作物，而不是生物强化主要作物。

paragraphs.text: In the bowels of CFF's third dome, lab manager Gomathy Sethuraman opens a window into the centre's "crown jewels", revealing vines of winged beans growing under a bright yellow light. It's one of multiple chambers where scientists are studying the impact of higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels on the nutritional make-up of alternative crops. This research is "the game changer", says Azam-Ali, ensuring that 'future crops' are also the healthiest ones in warmer climates.
paragraphs.translation: 在CFF第三个穹顶的深处，实验室经理Gomathy Sethuraman打开了中心"皇冠上的明珠"的一扇窗，揭示了在明亮黄光下生长的四棱豆藤蔓。这是多个研究室之一，科学家们正在研究更高温度和二氧化碳水平对替代作物营养组成的影响。这项研究是"游戏规则改变者，"Azam-Ali说，确保'未来作物'在更温暖的气候中也是最健康的。

paragraphs.text: There is a growing global momentum around forgotten foods, says Danielle Nierenberg, president of Food Tank, a US-based think tank. Other than CFF, which bills itself as the world's first research centre dedicated solely to under-utilised crops, there are other key groups championing agricultural diversity including Crop Trust, Slow Food, Icrisat and Bioversity International. Add to that more middle-income consumers searching for nutritious foods and others eager to try the unprocessed foods their grandparents once ate, she says.
paragraphs.translation: 美国智库Food Tank的总裁Danielle Nierenberg说，关于遗忘食品的全球势头正在增长。除了自称为世界上第一个专门致力于未充分利用作物的研究中心CFF外，还有其他关键团体倡导农业多样性，包括Crop Trust、Slow Food、Icrisat和Bioversity International。再加上更多中等收入消费者寻找营养食品，以及其他渴望尝试祖父母曾经吃的未加工食品的人，她说。

paragraphs.text: But the rising interest in forgotten foods in some quarters is overtaken by the global spread of Western-style diets heavy in sugar, fat and processed foods in others.
paragraphs.translation: 但某些地区对遗忘食品的兴趣上升，被其他地区高糖、高脂肪和加工食品的西方饮食全球传播所超越。

paragraphs.text: A key obstacle to promoting fading local crops in Malaysia, for example, is "the obsession with imported products", says Jenifer Kuala, co-founder of a restaurant that champions locally-sourced food in an affluent suburb of Kuala Lumpur. Customers at Sitka, regarded as a pioneer in the country's small farm-to-table dining scene, still seek foreign ingredients as a "status symbol", she says.
paragraphs.translation: 例如，在马来西亚推广衰退本地作物的一个关键障碍是"对进口产品的痴迷，"Jenifer Kuala说，她是吉隆坡富裕郊区一家倡导本地食材餐厅的联合创始人。Sitka被视为该国小型农场到餐桌餐饮场景的先驱，其顾客仍将外国食材视为"地位象征"，她说。

paragraphs.text: The argument for forgotten foods feels intuitive. Some analysts say it is in fact inevitable. "Climate change is going to mean almost certainly tastes are going to be forced to change," says Tim Lang, professor of food policy at City University of London. We "have to get used to eating other crops" as yields of staple crops fall, he says.
paragraphs.translation: 支持遗忘食品的论点感觉是直觉性的。一些分析师说，这实际上是不可避免的。"气候变化几乎肯定意味着口味将被迫改变，"伦敦城市大学食品政策教授Tim Lang说。随着主食作物产量下降，我们"必须习惯吃其他作物，"他说。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Imagine you're an alien sent to Earth to document the behaviour of the mammals inhabiting the planet. You stumble into a movie theatre that's showing the latest Hollywood horror film.
paragraphs.translation: 想象你是一名被派往地球记录该星球哺乳动物行为的外星人。你偶然走进一家正在上映最新好莱坞恐怖片的电影院。

paragraphs.text: Several dozen humans are gathered together in a dark, undecorated room. They're all staring at a rectangular area on which patterns of light change rapidly.
paragraphs.translation: 几十个人类聚集在一个黑暗、简陋的房间里。他们都盯着一个矩形区域，上面光影图案快速变化。

paragraphs.text: They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.
paragraphs.translation: 他们显然处于高度兴奋状态。心率升高，他们偶尔紧张地环顾四周，有时集体在座位上跳起来，并发出高音调的警告呼喊。

paragraphs.text: Eventually, the lights come up and the rectangular screen goes black. The humans stand up and leave the room, chatting and laughing, and showing signs of pleasure.
paragraphs.translation: 最终，灯光亮起，矩形屏幕变黑。人类站起来离开房间，谈笑风生，表现出愉悦的迹象。

paragraphs.text: Why do these humans voluntarily expose themselves to what appears to be a deeply unpleasant experience? And why do they react so strongly to those patterns of light on a screen?
paragraphs.translation: 为什么这些人类自愿将自己暴露在看似极其不愉快的经历中？又为什么他们对屏幕上那些光影图案反应如此强烈？

paragraphs.text: I am fascinated with the paradox of horror—the strange fact that many people seek out scary entertainment.
paragraphs.translation: 我对恐怖悖论深感着迷——许多人寻求恐怖娱乐这一奇怪事实。

paragraphs.text: I think the answer to the puzzle lies in human nature.
paragraphs.translation: 我认为这个谜题的答案在于人性。

paragraphs.text: My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context. You can see these elements of horror in children's games. Take hide-and-seek for example, which is a simulation of a predator-prey interaction. The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator, searching for the child while howling like a dangerous beast.
paragraphs.translation: 我的研究表明，人类进化成在安全情境中体验负面情绪时能找到乐趣。你可以在儿童游戏中看到恐怖元素的影子。以捉迷藏为例，它是捕食者-猎物互动的模拟。孩子躲藏，成人假装是捕食者，像危险野兽一样嚎叫着寻找孩子。

paragraphs.text: This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.
paragraphs.translation: 这种模拟为孩子提供了关于如何避免成为猎物的关键信息，孩子们往往觉得这类活动非常令人满足，大概是因为它让他们安全地体验潜在灾难性场景。

paragraphs.text: They find it pleasurable, and pleasure is evolution's way of motivating us toward adaptive behaviour.
paragraphs.translation: 他们觉得这很愉快，而愉快是进化激励我们采取适应性行为的方式。

paragraphs.text: Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.
paragraphs.translation: 恐怖对许多人来说是愉快的，因为它让我们玩弄负面情绪并发展应对策略。我们学会了真正害怕的感觉，也学会了如何处理负面情绪。

paragraphs.text: How, then, does horror work? My research suggests that horror works by exploiting an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms—an evolved fear system, which we share with other animals. But humans are uniquely imaginative, and we use our evolved imagination to travel into virtual worlds that are full of danger.
paragraphs.translation: 那么，恐怖是如何起作用的？我的研究表明，恐怖通过利用一套古老的生物防御机制——一种我们与其他动物共享的进化恐惧系统——来起作用。但人类具有独特的想象力，我们用进化而来的想象力进入充满危险的虚拟世界。

paragraphs.text: There are good reasons for watching a horror film, even if you're not a loyal horror fan. If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience. Anyway, watching a horror film makes you better at handling your own fear, and who knows when that will become critically relevant?
paragraphs.translation: 观看恐怖片有充分的理由，即使你不是忠实的恐怖迷。如果你完整地看完了电影，你可能会体验到一种强烈的掌控感，一种你能够度过可怕经历的感觉。总之，观看恐怖片能让你更好地处理自己的恐惧，谁知道这何时会变得至关重要呢？

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years. But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.
paragraphs.translation: 在物理世界中，一场觉醒正在发生，反对多年来强加给我们的美丽模式。但在数字领域，社交媒体决定了什么是美。

paragraphs.text: The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel. In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don't correspond to the so-called ideal. All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda, have become "legitimate." At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws.
paragraphs.translation: 两场对立的斗争正在并行进行。在物理世界中，这场斗争反对施加在女性身上、要求她们符合不切实际的美丽理想的潜在压力。作为斗争的一部分，各类媒体展示了身体不符合所谓理想的女性。所有那些曾被排除在杂志封面、电视剧和公共议程之外的女性，都变得“合法”了。同时，一群网红开始上传自己不化妆的照片，甚至上传突出所谓缺陷的照片。

paragraphs.text: Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses. One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the "cyborg look," which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050. The cyborg look spread rapidly. Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.
paragraphs.translation: 技术重塑了我们的美丽理想，并在向大众传达这一信息方面做得很好。过去十年的怪异遗产之一是“半机械人造型”的流行，它展示了2050年美国人将是什么样子。半机械人造型迅速传播。然而今天，Instagram脸已成为新的美丽理想。

paragraphs.text: The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process. The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified (游戏化的) interaction offered by the social media platforms—the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share.
paragraphs.translation: 当学习过程有积极参与时，接受美丽规范的内化会更有效。用户的积极参与体现在社交媒体平台提供的游戏化互动中——点赞、写评论、比较、分享的能力。

paragraphs.text: Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal such as editing the image, choosing the ideal filter, the right background.
paragraphs.translation: 一旦理想的美丽理想被内化，用户就会获得改变外观以适应接受的美丽理想的工具或功能，如编辑图像、选择理想的滤镜、合适的背景。

paragraphs.text: A survey conducted in the United States revealed that more than 50% filter the images before posting them. And you will not be surprised to hear that the majority of them are women. One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.
paragraphs.translation: 一项在美国进行的调查显示，超过50%的人在发布图像前会进行滤镜处理。听到其中大多数是女性，你不会感到惊讶。过度滤镜的一个重要后果是，出现了将自己视为被观察和评价的对象的倾向，就像另一个人从侧面观察和评判一样。

paragraphs.text: The effect of the filters is already far beyond amiable amusement. The filters and the entire game played on the networks affect the mental health of the users. According to a study, apps like Instagram, Snapchat and FaceTune allow users to achieve a level of perfection that was previously only observed in beauty magazines. Even though humanity has always cherished beauty, in the last decade our obsession with looks has reached an unprecedented peak. The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care.
paragraphs.translation: 滤镜的效果已远超出友好的娱乐。滤镜以及在网络上进行的整个游戏影响了用户的心理健康。根据一项研究，像Instagram、Snapchat和FaceTune这样的应用程序让用户达到了以前只在美容杂志中观察到的完美程度。尽管人类一直珍视美，但在过去十年中，我们对外表的痴迷达到了前所未有的高峰。在社交媒体上花费的时间催生了实现不可能的美丽理想的强烈冲动，以至于唯一能解决它的不是美容干预，而是心理健康护理。

questionGroups.sourceText: 北斗（Beidou）卫星导航系统的成功研制是中国自改革开放以来取得的一项重大科技成就。研发人员经过不懈努力，攻克了一系列技术难题，北斗系统最终实现了全球覆盖和高精度定位，使中国成为世界上少数几个独立拥有全球卫星导航系统的国家之一。北斗系统已广泛应用于交通运输、灾害救援、天气预报、公共安全等诸多领域。北斗系统现在已经在国际上得到广泛认可，开始为越来越多的国家和地区提供优质服务。

answer.modelTranslation: The successful development of the Beidou satellite navigation system represents a significant scientific and technological achievement for China since its reform and opening up. It has now gained international recognition and is providing quality services to an increasing number of countries and regions.
